strait-of-hormuz.summary: Effectively closed to normal commercial traffic since 28 Feb: Iran requires permits and fees through its Strait Authority, a US blockade of Iranian ports has been in force since 14 July, and attacks on ships continue. The IMO recorded 9 tanker attacks in the strait in the week of 28 Sep-5 Oct, the highest weekly total since the war began; a chemical tanker (Acers) was separately struck by projectiles on 7 Oct about 51 nautical miles off Qatar, west of the usual attack cluster, and Iran's IRGC said it struck the LPG tanker NV Sunshine on 9 Oct for taking an unauthorized route (IRGC claim, unverified). Reuters reported, citing officials close to Tehran, that Iran plans to widen threats against ships using routes it hasn't authorized, including Omani-side channels and Gulf of Oman transfer points — a plan that could not be independently verified. President Trump said on 8 Oct the US will not attack Iran before November's midterm elections, that the US blockade remains in force, and that oil is flowing through the strait; he rejected Iran's latest proposal to end the war. Saudi Aramco is in talks to formalize long-term shuttle contracts built on the ship-to-ship transfer system that bypasses the strait, and VLCC freight on the Gulf-to-Asia route hit a record near $1.4 million/day as that shuttle system strains vessel supply. Kpler ship-tracking data put Hormuz crude exports at about 8.5 mb/d (roughly 40% below pre-war) in the week to 7 Oct, down from the 13.2 mb/d (about 77% of baseline) Kpler reported for the week to 29 Sep, even as satellite imagery had shown a 'major operational recovery' at Saudi Arabia's Yanbu terminal; Vortexa separately put non-Iranian Gulf oil flows at 81% of pre-war levels in September. Tankers still move mainly under naval escort or shuttle arrangements rather than normal free transit, and many sail with transponders off, so independent counts remain partial. The attack zone widened further on 9 October when the fully laden VLCC GEM NO.2 was struck by an unidentified projectile about 13 nautical miles west of Al Jazeera, UAE, outside the strait itself; two more unnamed outbound tankers were then hit by projectiles and caught fire inside the strait on 10 and 11 October, per UKMTO, with crews reported safe in both cases. Iran's security chief Mohsen Rezaei said on 11 October that the US response to Iran's seven conditions for reopening the strait was ‘insufficient’ and that Tehran would stop responding through the current channel; the US had replied via Qatari intermediaries. Delayed UKMTO and JMIC reports disclosed on 12 Oct showed the 11 Oct toll was larger than first known: six vessels, five tankers and a container ship, were struck that day, the highest single-day total since the war began; one was hit by a drone at Oman's Sohar anchorage and reclassified from 'suspicious activity' to an attack, and JMIC raised its threat assessment for the strait to SEVERE. No group claimed responsibility for any of the six.

bab-el-mandeb.summary: The Houthis have enforced a 'ban' on Saudi-linked shipping since 20 July, hitting ships (Tihamah 12 Aug, Bahri VLCC off Yanbu 24 Aug) and seizing Mocha and Red Sea islands on 10-11 Sep. Tanker transits fell sharply; overall transits were ~15% below pre-ban levels by late August. Saudi-backed Yemeni government forces launched a counteroffensive ('Operation Yemen Dawn') around 3-5 Oct, backed by a reported 100 Saudi-led coalition jets, and said they had taken full control of the strait plus Dhubab town, its airport and the road to Mokha; on 9 Oct the Saudi-led coalition said it struck 136 further 'high-value' Houthi targets and Yemeni officials additionally claimed Mayyun (Perim) Island, which the Houthis had seized in September, had been retaken. On 10 Oct Houthi media said they repelled the Yemeni-government push on Mayyun and still hold the island, directly contradicting the 9 Oct claim. Both sides' claims are unverified and independent confirmation of territorial or shipping-lane control remains unavailable, so the status here is unchanged.

east-west-pipeline.summary: Shut 11 Sep after drone strikes on pumping stations (launched from Iraq); restarted around 21-22 Sep. Saudi Energy Minister Prince Abdulaziz bin Salman said on 6 Oct that flow had reached 5.8 million bpd — about 83% of its 7 mb/d capacity — with roughly 4 mb/d of that rerouted to Yanbu on the Red Sea to bypass Hormuz, about 4% of global oil supply. Flows were as low as ~2 mb/d in August (Kpler) after Houthi attacks on the Red Sea route. Aramco is also in talks to formalize long-term shuttle contracts built on this bypass system.

kharg-island.summary: The terminal was intact after US strikes on military targets (14 Mar). Iranian exports have been under a US naval blockade since 14 July, and the US struck an Iranian tanker off Kharg on 5 Sep. Tracking group United Against Nuclear Iran (UANI), corroborated by Bloomberg vessel-tracking, reported at least 50 Iranian tankers backed up along Iran's coast as of early October, 11 of them laden and anchored east of Kharg with none loading there on 5 Oct; Iran loaded no crude at all in September — the first such month since the war began — with exports falling from about 966,000 b/d in July to roughly 50,000 b/d, as no Iranian crude is known to have crossed the blockade line since 14 July.

gulf-of-mexico-offshore.summary: Hurricane Isaias made landfall near Destin, Florida, around 8pm ET on 9 October as a Category 2 storm and weakened to post-tropical by 10 October. BSEE's Marine Minerals Administration said shut-ins eased to about 68.76% of current Gulf oil output (about 1.40 million b/d) by midday 10 October, down from a peak of 71.51% on 9 October, with 113 of 371 manned platforms still evacuated (down from 129). Separately, DOE authorized an emergency Strategic Petroleum Reserve exchange of up to 4 million barrels (2 million each to ExxonMobil and BP) to support Gulf Coast refineries. Expected to be temporary; undamaged facilities resume production once post-storm inspections are complete.
